brief.topic: Four questions before you build an AI agent

coreInsight: Before building an agent, write its job description: the steps it owns, the tools it can touch, the actions that need human sign-off, and how its work is scored.

caption.opening: If you can’t write an agent’s job description, you’re not ready to build the agent.
body:
Four lines before any code:
→ Tasks: which steps does it own?
→ Tools: what can it read or change?
→ Sign-off: which actions need a human?
→ Review: how will you score its work?

“Handles support” isn’t a job. “Drafts refund replies for review, reads orders but can’t issue refunds, scored weekly on past tickets” is. If you can’t fill a line, narrow the job or build a plain workflow.

claims.text: Scoping an agent by its owned tasks, tool access, approval points and review method before building reduces risk and vague requirements.
